$comment: The Motion Shaper's parameters, declared once.
Both the C++ setter dispatch and the TypeScript control table are GENERATED
from this file by scripts/generate-params.mjs. Neither is hand-written and
neither may be hand-edited, which is what makes Ledger cell D1's first half
unconstructible rather than tested: a control that names no parameter cannot
be written down, and a parameter with no control cannot exist, because both
sides come out of this list.
A parity check between two hand-maintained tables is a test that passes for
a long time and then fails once, after the drift it existed to catch has
already shipped. Across fourteen units that is fourteen chances. This is the
same move as WetDryMixer's branded latency and the seqlock publish path.
`apply` is the C++ that routes one real-world value into the unit. It is
spelled out per parameter rather than inferred from the symbol, because a
rule that guesses `setFoo` from `Foo` breaks the first time a parameter sets
one field of a struct — which here is every band control. `delta` is the
pair of values D1's render-delta half sets to prove the setter reaches audio.

params.name: Bands
params.note: The control is a choice index and the unit counts bands from one, so the +1 is the mapping and not an off-by-one.

params.name: Low / Mid
params.note: Both corners go in together because they are one filter network; the other one is read back rather than remembered here.

params.name: Slope
params.apply:
const int i = static_cast<int>(v + 0.5);
        u.setSlope(i <= 0 ? dsp::Slope::Db6 : (i == 1 ? dsp::Slope::Db12 : dsp::Slope::Db24));

params.note: Sixteenths, which is what the sheet's swing control shifts; the unit exposes the amount and fixes the grid rather than shipping two controls that only make sense together.
